text:
ana_support: raising thread — multiple customers in eu1 reporting embed API p95/p99 regressions starting ~02:10 UTC after the overnight infra push. Customer ACME shows p99 ~900ms (was ~120ms).
ops_bot: alert created: INC-2026-314 (links: https://redwood/inc/INC-2026-314) :rotating_light:
ashley_sre: looking. any host-level spikes in iowait or CPU?
nana_support: quick snapshot from ACME run: 'embed' calls to model-x show big tail on put/get to /dev/nvme0n1.
kevin_infra: we pushed CUDA 12.2.1 + driver 535.54 to eu1 pool at 01:50 UTC. rolling update completed 02:05 UTC.
mike_runtime: that lines up. suspect driver+nvme interrupt handling causing host I/O noise and KV cache stalls.
lucy_devex: repro steps we asked ACME for: 1) single 128-dim embed batch of 64; 2) seq len 512 tokens for chat; 3) spike reproducible ~5-20% of requests.
nashley_sre: can someone grep the node kernel logs for nvme errors and firmware messages? try:
```
journalctl -k -u nvme -S "2026-03-17 01:40" --no-pager | tail -n 200
dmesg | grep -i nvme
```
kevin_infra: pulled logs from host-213: repeated nvme timeout resets around 02:03 UTC, also a few "nvme0: reset controller" entries. attaching snippet:
```
[ 02:03:12.345678] nvme nvme0: I/O 9 timed out, aborting
[ 02:03:12.346789] nvme nvme0: reset controller
[ 02:03:13.123456] nvme nvme0: firmware revision 1.2.3
```
mike_runtime: that pattern matches driver interrupt storm we saw in staging with 535.x on certain firmware versions. immediate mitigations: 1) revert driver to previous package on eu1; 2) move affected tenants to fallback pool (usw2) using routing policy; 3) enable software KV cache TTL extension to reduce NVMe QPS.
nana_support: customers asking for ETA — what's safe short-term rollback plan?
kevin_infra: we can rollback driver package across the pool in ~20m with a rolling reboot per node. risk: brief connection drops but will remove the nvme resets.
nashley_sre: I can start routing rule to divert embed traffic for impacted orgs to dedicated fallback model in usw2. lucy, can we also flip a per-tenant cache TTL?
lucy_devex: yes — toggle the runtime config key `runtime.kv_cache.extended_ttl=true` via console for the tenant. I'll prepare the runbook snippet.
ops_bot: runbook link: https://redwood/runbooks/infra-nvme-driver-rollback
oncall_pm: prioritize rollback + routing. notify SOC and account team for ACME.
nana_support: ACME notified, they asked for keepalive while you perform rollback.
kevin_infra: kicking off driver rollback on canary subset (host-213, host-219) now. watching host logs and load balancer error rates.
mike_runtime: adding a temporary auto-fallback policy to route requests failing >500ms to model-y in usw2 for 30m. config:
```
{
  "policy": "latency_fallback",
  "threshold_ms": 500,
  "fallback_region": "usw2",
  "duration_minutes": 30
}
```
nashley_sre: after rollback on host-213 we see nvme resets stop and p99 on that host drops from ~920ms to ~140ms. beginning pool-wide rollback.
nana_support: ACME reports better tail latency for their tests. :thumbsup:
lucy_devex: patch note for customers: sending brief status update to affected orgs and redwood status page.
kevin_infra: full rollback complete at 03:10 UTC. monitoring for 30m.
mike_runtime: metrics show overall eu1 embed p99 reduced from 780ms -> 160ms, p95 from 220ms -> 110ms. KV cache hit rate increased ~12%.
oncall_pm: closing incident once 30m stable. please paste postmortem links and mitigation follow-ups here.
nashley_sre: immediate follow-ups: schedule firmware compatibility test with 535 driver, add kernel nvme counters to our SLO dashboards, add a preflight check to rolling driver updates to detect nvme reset spikes, and update runbook to include TTL tuning as mitigation.
lucy_devex: I'll draft customer-facing note and update status page draft.
nana_support: thanks team — ACME happy for now. saving logs & timeline to INC-2026-314.
ops_bot: incident INC-2026-314 status -> resolved (monitoring) at 03:40 UTC :white_check_mark:
